problem: Decide, for each customer refund request, whether to refund automatically or send it to a person, and draft the reply that tells the customer.

fit.reason: The order number, the amount paid and the delivery time are values written in the message that extraction reads; whether the customer says the goods arrived broken is a judgment about reading; the claim history is a lookup code already has; the reply is written text.

decisions.description: Refund the order automatically, or send the request to a person to review.

costs.false_positive: Money is returned for an order that did not deserve a refund.
costs.false_negative: A customer with a valid small claim waits for a person to read it.

message.description: The refund request message as the customer typed it.

deterministic.description: The customer has had three or more refunds in the past year.
deterministic.computed_by: count refunds for the account id in the refund ledger

extract.instructions: The total amount the customer paid for the order, in dollars.
extract.purpose: A small order refunds in code with no model call, so the amount has to be a number code can compare.

extract.instructions: The order number exactly as the customer wrote it.
extract.purpose: The reply names the order, and a copied value is checked against the message.

extract.instructions: How many days the delivery took or is expected to take, counted from the order date.
extract.purpose: A delivery that ran two weeks late refunds on its own; the interval says how sure the estimate is.

derive.purpose: A very expensive order that took only a few days to arrive is read by a person; code divides the two extracted values, and the result is null when the delivery estimate is missing or zero.

questions.instructions: The customer says the goods arrived damaged.
questions.purpose: Separates a damage claim, which a small order refunds, from a delivery complaint or a change of mind.

threshold.why: An automatic refund needs a confident yes, because a refund sent in error cannot be recalled.

refund.why: A customer with a history of refunds is always read by a person.
An order of twenty dollars or less refunds without a question, decided on the extracted amount alone.
A delivery that took at least two weeks even on the optimistic end of the estimate refunds.
An order that cost over a thousand dollars per delivery day is read by a person before it refunds.
A confident damage claim on an order of two hundred dollars or less refunds.

escalation.description: Nothing escalates: the default sends an unclear request to a person.

write.purpose: The text that tells the customer what happens to their request.
write.instructions: Write a two-sentence reply to the customer. Name the order and say whether the refund is on its way or a person will read the request.

ground_truth.source: the refund the support lead approved or declined after reading the request

calibration.promotion: Enforce only after the damage question clears its threshold on at least 100 labelled requests with balanced accuracy at or above 0.85.

provenance.notes: Synthetic refund-triage system used to test the v2 pipeline runner.
